headline: HEXACHLOR SPILL POISONS GEARTOWN CANAL — RESIDENTS ORDERED TO EVACUATE
body:
A ruptured storage tank at the Ironclad Processing Facility on Geartown's South Industrial Row released an estimated 180,000 liters of hexachlorobenzene compound into the Geartown Canal early Tuesday morning, prompting a mandatory evacuation of eighteen residential blocks and triggering a health emergency that district officials say may affect up to 22,000 residents. The spill, caused by what Ironclad described as a 'pressure failure in an aging containment system,' began at approximately 2:10 AM and was not reported to city environmental monitors until 5:40 AM — a three-and-a-half-hour delay that Shelf Voice sources say was used to attempt internal containment before notifying authorities. By the time evacuation orders went out, canal water had reached residential drainage systems in at least four blocks.

Geartown residents — many of whom work the night shift at the very facilities now poisoning their neighborhood — described scenes of chaos as families fled with whatever they could carry. 'My kids were already sick when the sirens went,' said resident Naomi Ferreira-Cho, whose two children were admitted to Geartown Mercy Clinic with respiratory symptoms. 'They knew. They knew for hours and they said nothing.' Ironclad's communications office released a statement attributing the delay to 'internal assessment protocols' and expressed 'deep regret' for any harm caused.

Environmental health teams from Helix Biosystems — contracted by the city on an emergency basis — are currently testing canal water, soil, and air quality across a two-kilometer radius. Early readings show hexachlorobenzene concentrations at 340 times the safe exposure threshold in the canal itself, and 12 times threshold in surface drainage water reaching residential areas. Long-term exposure to the compound is linked to liver damage, neurological degradation, and elevated cancer risk. Geartown's population, already among the most economically precarious in Meridian, has almost no access to private healthcare.

City Council representative Kwame Osei-Johanssen called for an immediate independent investigation into the delay, but stopped short of demanding Ironclad face criminal sanction. 'What I want to know,' he said at a press conference outside Geartown Mercy, 'is how a company can watch poison pour into a neighborhood for three and a half hours and call it assessment.'
aftermath: Ironclad was fined 14 million quanta by the Environmental Directorate — a figure critics noted was less than 2% of the corponation's quarterly profits — and the canal remained officially closed for eight years, though residents reported it was used informally throughout that period.
casualties: 14 confirmed hospitalizations, 22,000 at elevated health risk, 2 deaths attributed within 30 days
runner_relevance: The spill generated immediate runner demand on multiple fronts. Community advocates and legal groups hired runners to retrieve Ironclad's internal incident logs and communications from the three-and-a-half-hour window before reporting — data retrieval contracts worth 3,000-7,000 quanta that Ironclad's own security teams were simultaneously trying to suppress or destroy. Smuggling contracts surged as displaced Geartown residents needed food, medicine, and clean water moved into the evacuation zone through unofficial channels. Helix Biosystems hired protection runners to guard their testing teams from Ironclad-affiliated intimidators. Whistleblowers inside Ironclad needed secure courier services to move documents to the Lake Monitor without being traced.
